about: What a filter condition's typed operand reads as, and the text an operand reopens in (ADR-0023, ADR-0006's note of 2026-10-01; tickets 94, 96, 97, 98), under a culture: C#'s FilterPanelChoices.ReadOperand, OperandText and RefusalText, and the Script Core's chrome/operand-reading.ts under ADR-0370 section 10's locale. From tests/ExGrid.Tests/OperandReadingTests.cs, DateOperandReadingTests.cs and DateTypeOperandReadingTests.cs; the rows where C#'s DateTime.TryParse reads what the Script Core refuses (a month's name, a 12-hour clock, a two-digit year) stay there, and so does ja-JP's 13/01/2026, which .NET's parser refuses before ticket 97's rule reads the one order that is a date. A case either reads (`reads`, the value; null for no operand) or is `refused` by kind, with the two `readings` of readsTwoWays and what was `read` for notTheColumnsDateForm; `says` is the built-in refusal's words. An `operandText` case gives the text a value reopens in, and `readsBack` the column type it is read back as, to the same value.
